steps.notes: Gold passes 4/4; independent clean-room textbook implementation (vectorized ideal LPF, center m//2, strict <) also passes 4/4. Wrong impls (identity, zeros, high-pass) all fail. Alternative conventions tested: geometric center (m-1)/2, <= inequality, unshifted T, fftfreq cycles/pixel units -- all fail, but the canonical fft2->fftshift->mask->ifftshift->ifft2 pipeline (strongly hinted by required_dependencies importing fftshift/ifftshift and by the explicit strict-inequality sentence in the prompt) is the natural expert reading.

findings.evidence: Docstring: 'frequency_threshold: float, the radius within which frequencies are preserved.' No unit is stated anywhere in prompt/background. The frozen target encodes radius in DFT-bin (pixel) units of the fftshifted spectrum, i.e. cycles per full image (gold: sqrt((i-m/2)**2+(j-n/2)**2) < frequency_threshold). A solver reading 'frequency' as normalized cycles/pixel (np.fft.fftfreq convention) fails: verified dynamically -- 'normalized_cycles_per_pixel' variant FAILs tests 1-3 (with thresholds 20-50 it becomes an all-pass filter). Test-case magnitudes (20, 40, 50 on 200x200/800x800 images) disambiguate, but solvers do not see test cases. Mitigation: the pixel-radius ideal-LPF is the overwhelming textbook default (Gonzalez-Woods) and required_dependencies importing fftshift/ifftshift signal the centered-spectrum pipeline, so a competent solver almost certainly picks the intended reading.
findings.suggested_fix: In the docstring change to: 'frequency_threshold: float, the radius (in pixels of the fft-shifted frequency grid, i.e. DFT bins) within which frequencies are preserved.'

findings.evidence: Test 4 contains a copy-paste bug: it builds 'image_array2 = np.tile(matrix, (400, 200))' from the second matrix but then calls 'T2, filtered_image2 = apply_low_pass_filter(image_array, frequency_threshold2)' -- passing the FIRST image, not image_array2 ('image_array1' and 'image_array2' are dead variables). No scoring impact because the assertion only uses T1/T2, and T depends only on the input shape (both 800x800), but the test does not exercise what its setup implies. Also note the assert '((3.1415925*(f1**2-f2**2)-MaskAreaDiff)/MaskAreaDiff<0.01) == target' is one-sided (a too-large mask making the expression negative also passes); tests 1-3 fully pin T elementwise, so this weakness is redundant rather than score-flipping.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the second call's argument with image_array2 (or drop the unused image_array1/image_array2 assignments), and use abs(...)<0.01 for a two-sided area check.

findings.evidence: Background text: 'The filter takes input image in size of [m,n] and the frequency threshold. Ouput the nxn array as the filtered image.' The output for an [m,n] input is m x n (gold returns shape (m,n)), not 'nxn'. Cosmetic contradiction only; all test images happen to be square (200x200, 800x800) so no score impact.
findings.suggested_fix: Change background to 'Output the m x n array as the filtered image.'

overall_assessment: Problem 6 is fair to score as-is. The single step is solvable from the prompt: the gold and an independently written textbook ideal low-pass filter both pass all 4 tests, the strict-inequality convention is explicitly stated, and the binary mask target T exactly pins the intended convention while rejecting all tested wrong implementations and plausible misreadings. The only real risk is the unstated unit of frequency_threshold (pixel-radius in the shifted spectrum), which the canonical reading resolves; remaining findings are cosmetic doc/test sloppiness with no scoring impact.
